These are made known and presented in a celebration to Ahura Mazda and various divine beings and spirits—Sraosha (Obedience), Ashi (Recompense), Rashnu the most just, Mithra of the wide pastures, the Bountiful Immortals, the Fravashis and souls of the saints, the Fire of Ahura Mazda, a lofty lord (Apam-napat?), Myazda, and the personified well‑timed prayer—for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and adoration of the entire holy creation. The rite is further dedicated to the Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitama, to the Fravashi of Anghuyu, and to all holy Fravashis of saints, dead, living, and unborn, including prophets who will serve by bringing on the renovation of the completed world. The Bountiful Immortals are praised as ever-living, ever-helpful rulers who dispose all things aright, bestow good, and dwell with—and arise from—the Good Mind. The celebrations are said to promote and benefit \"this house\" by increasing the household, overcoming restrictions and harmful malice, and blessing its herds, retainers, and saints (male and female), who are described as Saoshyants of the provinces through their good deeds. The good Fravashis of the saints are described as formidable and overwhelming in aid, and Sraosha is invoked again at the Section V then offers sacrifice to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, personified powers of force and victory, the path of pleasantness, the good lake Zarenumawt, the \"Glowing\" Mountain made by Mazda, and all the Yazads. Section VI is a propitiatory formula directed to the body and soul of the Kine of blessed endowment—whether one cow, several, or a herd—used when milk is drawn for an offering and water is taken to wash the udder. Section VII offers sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise to the good waters created by Mazda, to the lofty lord Apam-napai, and to the Ahurian One of Ahura, with vows to utter praises, complete good sacrifices with appropriate gifts among the holy Yazads, pour out the water, and recite the lofty Gathas belonging to the ritual.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The speaker calls for foes to disappear so that the dead may arise unhindered and bodily life THE  GAH   HAVAN2. / GAH    III.  383; lines 20194-20283","start":"20194","end":"20283","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Liturgical passages for the Gahs describe a worshipper who blesses and sacrifices to Asha Vahishta (Righteousness), the Fire as Ahura Mazda's son, Ahura Mazda, Apam-napat, Mazda-created waters, various ritual lords, heavenly bodies, doctrinal proclamations, manifest truth, later lore, and holy creation, while repeatedly confessing Mazdayasnian faith, allegiance to Zarathustra's order, and enmity toward the Daevas. The Uzayeirina and Aiwisruthrima prayers are noted as daily recitations at their respective hours.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Asha Vahishta, identified as \"Righteousness the Best,\" and the Fire, described as Ahura Mazda's son, are invoked together at the start of the passage.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The Fire, Ahura Mazda's son, is called \"the holy ritual lord\" and receives sacrifice from the worshipper.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The speaker blesses the sacrifice, homage, strength, and swiftness of Asha Vahishta and of the Fire of Ahura Mazda, and ascribes glory to one of them.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The worshipper offers propitiation to Ahura Mazda and states that Asha Vahishta is a blessing.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The worshipper confesses to being a Mazdayasnian of Zarathustra's order, a foe to the Daevas, and devoted to the lore of the Lord.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise are dedicated to Uzayeirina, Frada-vira, and Dacyuma, who are called holy lords of the ritual order.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Apam-napat, described as a lofty Ahura, and the waters which Mazda created receive sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Uzayeirina, Zaotar, Havanan, Atarevakhsha, Frabaretar, Abere/, Asnatar, Raethwukar, and Sraoshavareza are listed as holy lords of the ritual order who receive sacrifice.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Sacrifices are offered to Frada-vira and Dacyuma, to the stars, the moon, the sun, the constellations, the stars without beginning, and to the glory of doctrinal proclamations described as the evil man's distress.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The manifest performer of the truth, glossed as the correct maintainer of the rites, is called a holy lord of the ritual order and receives sacrifice.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Later lore, the manifest fulfiller of the truth, and the entire creation of the holy and the clean by day and night, together with Zaothras and offered prayers, receive sacrifice and homage in connection with Dacyuma.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Dacyuma is called \"the lord\" and \"holy lord of the ritual order\" and is a focus of sacrifice and homage.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"Apam-napat is further characterized as a lofty and royal lord, brilliant, and \"of the fleet horses,\" and receives sacrifice along with the Mazda-made holy water.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"The Fire, again called Ahura Mazda's son, receives sacrifice, and the speaker blesses the sacrifice, homage, strength, and swiftness of Apam-napat and of the waters which Mazda created.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"In the Aiwisruthrima gAh, the speaker again propitiates Ahura Mazda, calls Asha Vahishta a blessing, repeats the confession of Mazdayasnian identity and hostility to the Daevas, and dedicates sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise to Aiwisruthrima, content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l7564-l7611","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    XLIII.  IO5 / I06  THE    GATHAS. / YASNA    XLIV. / IOS  THE    GATHAS.; lines 7564-7611","start":"7564","end":"7611","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"\"religion of 'Falsehood'\" and \"the holy truth\" are contrasted, and the Spirit is praised as foremost of Heaven.","summary":"Mills' commentary on a section of the Gathas describes the composer beseeching Ahura to speak and reveal holy truth, in contrast to the falsifying utterance of an opposing 'religion of Falsehood.' The composer asks how to offer proper homage and by what ceremonial and grace the bountiful Spirit, the foremost one of Heaven and effectively identical with Mazda, may be conciliated and drawn near. This Spirit is praised as a guardian who has held off destruction from believing saints and repentant men, as first father of the personified holy Order (Asha) by generation, and as the one who fixed the undeviating path of stars and sun and underlies laws of gravitation and atmospheric phenomena like winds and clouds. The commentary highlights the personified Immortals Asha and Good Mind, noting that Good Mind is a created immortal thought while Asha is said to be born, and briefly mentions a recognition of the satisfactions of energetic life and the solaces of slumber.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The composer beseeches Ahura to speak to him and to reveal, as is His habit, \"the holy truth.\"","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Ahura's characteristic manner of speaking is contrasted with the falsifying utterance of an opposing religion described as the 'religion of Falsehood.'","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The first question the composer asks is how he may offer homage, including the homage of God Himself or of His bountiful Spirit.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The composer asks Ahura to show by what ceremonial he may conciliate Him and by what helps of grace the Spirit, or Ahura Himself, may be inclined to draw near in response to his frequent prayer.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The composer again asks how he may serve that Spirit as the foremost one of Heaven, who seeks an addition of praise to praise.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The Spirit, compared to Ahura in another place, is described as a guardian who has held off destruction from all believing saints and from all repentant men, while being both chief of Heaven and a benignant friend.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The composer addresses Mazda, saying of the Spirit that \"He is indeed Thyself,\" identifying the Spirit with Mazda.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The composer asks who was the first father of \"our holy Order\" as a personified Immortal, said to arise not by creation but by generation, as a parent generates a child.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"The composer asks who fixed for the stars and sun the undeviating \"way\" or path through space, which their fathers had long observed as non-random.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The commentator states that the laws of gravitation then become the theme of the composer's praise, still expressed in the form of questions, along with atmospheric phenomena such as clouds driven by winds.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The clouds driven by winds are said to be terrible, and the commentator compares them by saying they are not like the Maruts beyond the mountains, although winds can still be terrible.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"The composer is described as turning from sublime natural objects to a spiritual power, the strength of righteous character, which he designates as the 'Good Mind.'","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"Good Mind is described as a great Immortal and immortal thought that is 'created,' in contrast to Asha, who in the referenced verse is called 'born.'","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"The commentary indicates that the composer recognizes the satisfactions of energetic life and the solaces of slumber as complementary through their contrast, although the sentence is incomplete.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Composer of the Gathas","description":"The unnamed composer who beseeches Ahura, asks questions about homage, service, cosmic order, and moral qualities.","role_refs":["role:1","role:10"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:2","ev:3","ev:4","ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Ahura / Mazda","description":"The deity addressed by the composer, associated with revealing holy truth, described as chief of Heaven and a benignant friend.","role_refs":["role:2","role:6"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:2","ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Bountiful Spirit / foremost one of Heaven","description":"The bountiful Spirit of Ahura, called the foremost one of Heaven and identified with Mazda, who seeks additional praise and acts as guardian.","role_refs":["role:3","role:6"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:2","ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Opposing religion of Falsehood","description":"An opposing religion characterized by falsifying utterance and described as the 'religion of Falsehood.'","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"Believing saints","description":"Believing saints guardian Spirit has held off destruction.","role_refs":["role:5"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"fig:7","name_or_label":"Holy Order / Asha","description":"\"Our holy Order\" personified as an content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l14223-l14324","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    X.  241 / YASNA    X.  243 / YASNA   XI. / YASNA    XL  245; lines 14223-14324","start":"14223","end":"14324","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"“Childless be thou, shorn of offspring, evil-famed, and slander-followed, who … dost not pray me swiftness … Holy Haoma … far from death … grant to me … the best world of the saints, shining, all brilliant.”","summary":"A hymn-like passage links the proper treatment of animals and the sacred drink Haoma with blessings, and neglect with curses. A voice curses the person who misuses fodder and fattens an animal only for personal gain. A horse speaks to its rider, warning against overdriving racers without prayer. Haoma itself addresses its drinker, cursing the one who withholds Haoma’s full outpouring while insisting it is holy and not a head-smiter, but far from death. The speaker recalls that his father once gave an offering whose tongue and left eye Ahura chose as a meal-portion for Haoma, granted by Mazda. Anyone who denies this portion will lack worthy descendants such as fire-priests, warriors, and farmers; instead evil offspring named Dahakas and Murakas will be born. Worshippers are urged to cut off Haoma’s flesh-portion quickly, lest Haoma bind them as he bound the Turanian robber-king Frangrasyan in iron in the mid-third of the earth, reflecting a threefold division of the world. Zarathustra then praises Haoma as a good creation of Mazda. A numerological or liturgical sequence describes ones, twos, threes up to nine in ten who zealously serve. The ritual notes describe the Raspi handing the Haoma-cup or vessel to the officiating priest. Finally, the worshipper offers his own mature person to holy, effective Haoma, associated with sacred exhilaration, and asks Haoma, who drives death afar, to grant the best shining world of the saints.","language":"English","quote_policy":"quoted"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"A voice pronounces a curse of childlessness, loss of offspring, and bad reputation on someone who does not use fodder fairly but fattens the speaker for wife, children, or a selfish meal.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"A horse speaks to its rider, warning him not to overdrive racing horses or stride across the fleetest unless he prays for the horse’s swiftness in crowded contests.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Haoma addresses its drinker, cursing the one who withholds Haoma from full outpouring and likening such a person to a skull-crushing robber, while declaring that Haoma is not a head-smiter and is holy and far from death.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:13"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The speaker says that his father gave an offering whose tongue and left eye Ahura chose and set apart as Haoma’s meal.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The text states that someone who denies Haoma this offering instead eats it himself or seeks to reclaim it, even though Mazda gave this tongue and left eye to bless Haoma as its portion.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"It is declared that in the house of the one who denies This faith is called Ahura’s Faith, the Zarathustrian creed, and the Mazdayasnian belief, and all good is ascribed to Ahura Mazda. content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l14023-l14120","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    IX.  237 / YASNA    IX.  239 / YASNA    X. / YASNA    X.  241; lines 14023-14120","start":"14023","end":"14120","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"\"Haoma grows while he is praised, and the man who praises him is therewith more victorious.\"","summary":"A devotee addresses Haoma, a sacred plant and drink, urging it to grow through his praise and describing its powers. Even slight pressing, praise, or tasting of Haoma’s juice smites the Daevas and removes wasting and foulness from the house where it is borne and praised. Unlike other intoxicants that go with violent Rapine, Haoma’s power is linked with friendship and gentle drunkenness, and it heals those who treat it tenderly. The speaker asks Haoma for shares of its healing virtues and victorious powers, promising faithful praise, which the Lord has decreed better even than \"Righteousness the Best.\" A well-skilled Deity created Haoma swift and wise and planted it on high Haraiti; bounteous birds carry it to extreme mountain summits, gorges, abysses, and snow-peaks. There Haoma grows in many kinds, milky white and golden, flowing with healing liquors that inspire the pious and protect the speaker from a curser’s death-aim and a maligner’s thought. Haoma is praised for making the poor man’s thoughts as great as those of the richest and as when mind culminates, and for endowing the man who drinks it with milk with retainers, prosperity, and mind. The devotee prays that Haoma’s exhilarations not vanish like milk-drops in the rain, calls Haoma holy and bearer of ritual truth, offers his well-grown body as a gift before it, and vehemently renounces the murderous woman Caini’s emptiness.","language":"English","quote_policy":"quoted"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The speaker prays to Haoma to grow on all its stems, branches, and shoots, and to increase through the speaker’s word.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Haoma is said to grow while he is praised.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The man who praises Haoma becomes more victorious.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Even the lightest pressure, feeblest praise, or slightest tasting of Haoma’s juice is said to avail for the \"thousand-smiting\" of the Daevas.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"When Haoma is borne to a house and his praise is truly sung there, wasting and foulness vanish from that house.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Haoma is described as a drink that is famed and health-bringing.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"All other toxicants are said to go hand in hand with \"Rapine of the bloody spear,\" but Haoma’s stirring power goes hand in hand with friendship, and his drunkenness is described as light.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Whoever caresses Haoma as a tender son receives Haoma’s healing presence to their body.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Haoma is said to possess healing virtues that make him a healer and victorious powers that make him a victor.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The speaker asks Haoma to grant him some of these healing virtues and victorious powers and promises to birds, taught by implanted instinct, carry Haoma to the Peaks-above-the-eagles, the mount’s extremest summit, gorges, abysses, heights of many pathways, and ever-whitened snow-peaks.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"The settings where Haoma is carried and grows are described as high mountain features: Peaks-above-the-eagles, mountain summits, gorges, abysses, many paths, and snow-peaks.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:7","ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"On these ranges Haoma grows in many kinds, sometimes of effective.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]},{"id":"obs:20","text":"Haoma is called holy and \"bearer of the ritual truth.\"","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]},{"id":"obs:21","text":"The speaker says he would cast his well-grown body before and around Haoma as a fit content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l18011-l18097","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    LXVIII.  321 / YASNA    LXVIII.  323 / YASNA    LXX.  325 / YASNA    LXXI.  327; lines 18011-18097","start":"18011","end":"18097","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"In the concluding section of the Yasna, the holy Frashacstra asks saintly, most eminent Zarathustra to explain what truly constitutes the memorised recital of the rites and the completed delivery of the Gathas. The formula continues with sacrifice to Ahura Mazda and worship of his entire body, the Bountiful Immortals, all ritual lords, the entire Mazdayasnian Faith, and the sacred metres. It praises the entire bounteous Mathra, the system of the Faith set up against the Daevas with its complete and long descent, all holy Yazads both heavenly and earthly, and the Fravashis of the saints. It further worships all holy creatures Mazda created that possess holy institutions, nature, lore, and sacrifice, and are to be worshipped by the holy, as well as all five holy Gathas and the entire Yasna with its flow, ebb, and sounding chants. Finally, it sacrifices to all praises of the Yasna and to all words spoken by Mazda, which are described as most fatal to evil thoughts, words, and deeds, designating these evils and then cutting down and felling every evil thought, word, and deed.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Frashacstra, described as holy, asks Zarathustra what content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l16649-l16735","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    XLII.  29I / YASNA    LIV.  293 / YASNA    LV.  295 / YASNA    LVII.  297; lines 16649-16735","start":"16649","end":"16735","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Hymnic and liturgical verses (Srosh Yast) praise the divinity Sraosha (Obedience) as blessed, stately, victorious, and lord of ritual order. Worshippers ask him to be present at their rites and to aid them, and they worship him together with good waters, the Bountiful Immortals, Blessedness, Righteousness, Nairya-sangha, and Ahura Mazda. Sraosha is described as the incarnate word of reason whose body is the Mathra, armed with a spear, and as the first to adore Ahura, the Bountiful Immortals, and the protector and Creator who create all things. The ritual is performed with the Yasna of the Yazads and consecrated waters. The text also honors the words and deeds of Zarathustra. Translator’s notes comment on Sraosha as an abstract quality of listening obedience, his antiquity, his role in finding the way to Ahura’s throne, and clarify that Angra Mainyu could not be the protector or creator mentioned.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Worshippers ask Sraosha, described as good, to be present for the worship of the good waters, the good and bountiful Immortals, and Blessedness the good, who is closely knit with the Righteous Order.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Sraosha is described as blessed and stately, one who smites with victory, furthers the settlements in their advance, and is the holy lord of the ritual order.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"\"Righteousness (called) the Best\" is described as a blessing.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Sraosha is called Obedience, blessed, mighty, the incarnate word of reason whose body is the Mathra, \"him of the daring spear,\" devoted to the Lord, and the object of sacrificial worship, homage, propitiation, and praise.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The translator notes that Sraosha is the only divinity of the later groups mentioned in the first four Gathas and suggests that this Yast is next in antiquity after the Gathic pieces.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The same note states that Sraosha’s name has not lost its meaning as an abstract quality, and that worshippers originally praised listening obedience or repentance and other abstract qualities along with their principal prayers and hymns.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Referring to Y. XXVIII, 6, the note says that Sraosha \"finds the way\" to Ahura or \"finds His throne.\"","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The hymn states that Sraosha, in the creation of Mazda, was the first to adore Ahura, doing so with the Baresman spread.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Sraosha is said to have worshipped the Bountiful Immortals first and to have worshipped both the protector and the Creator, who are both creating all things in the creation.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Sraosha is worshipped for his splendour, glory, might, and victorious blow with the Yasna of the Yazads, a Yasna loud intoned, together with consecrated waters, good Blessedness, and Nairya-sangha.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The worshippers ask Sraosha, who smites with victory, to draw near to them to aid them.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"The text declares worship of Sraosha and of the lofty Lord who is Ahura Mazda Himself, who has attained the most to the ritual and has approached nearest to the worshippers in their celebrations.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"The worshippers also honor all the words of Zarathustra and all deeds well done for him, including those done in times gone by.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"The translator’s note on the \"protector\" and \"Creator\" suggests that Ahura and one of the Immortals, or possibly Zarathustra, may be meant, and states that Angra Mainyu could not have been worshipped as either protector or creator.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Sraosha (Obedience)","description":"Divine being identified with Obedience, described as blessed, stately, mighty, the incarnate word of reason whose body is the Mathra, armed with a daring spear, smiting with victory, furthering settlements, ruling as lord of the ritual order, first adoring Ahura and worshipping the Bountiful Immortals and the protector and Creator, and asked to draw near to aid worshippers.","role_refs":["role:1","role:2","role:3","role:4","role:12"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:2","ev:3","ev:4","ev:5","ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Ahura Mazda","description":"Lofty Lord identified as Ahura Mazda, recipient of Sraosha’s first adoration at the creation of Mazda, described as having a throne to which Sraosha may find the way, and as the Lord who has attained the most to the ritual and approached nearest to worshippers in their celebrations.","role_refs":["role:5"],"evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:4","ev:6"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Good waters","description":"The good waters that are worshipped together with Sraosha and are present in the form of consecrated waters used in the Yasna.","role_refs":["role:8"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Bountiful Immortals","description":"Good and bountiful Immortals who are worshipped and are said to have been first worshipped by Sraosha.","role_refs":["role:8"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:4"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"Blessedness","description":"Personified \"Blessedness the good,\" closely knit with the Righteous Order, described as good and lofty, and invoked together with Sraosha and consecrated waters in the ritual.","role_refs":["role:7","role:8"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:6","name_or_label":"Righteousness the Best","description":"\"Righteousness (called) the Best,\" described as a The Ratu pronounces a blessing on a servant of the Lord, wishing him what is better than the good and a reward like that of the Zaotar, who advances in good thoughts, words, and deeds, and the Zaotar replies with a reciprocal blessing. The text affirms an excellent Ahu and Ratu who rule from righteousness, and mentions sacrifice to the Ahuna-vairya formula, to Asha Vahishta, to the Fshusho-mathra, and to the collection of Yasna praises instituted in the world of old. Yasna LX then offers prayers (noted as used when a travelling priest visits farm-houses) that one who shows straight paths of profit for bodily and mental life in the eternal realms where Ahura dwells may approach and be blessed, and that the sacrificer’s house and village receive wise perceptions of saints, ritual blessings, guilelessness, recognition of what is due, righteous order, divine sovereign power, lasting prominence of the Zarathustrian religion, and the speedy presence of kine in the deeds.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The Zaotar replies with a corresponding blessing, wishing that what is better than the good happen to the other and that The hymn requests heaven and legitimate offspring. It includes sacrifice to the Ahurian One, the cosmic sea Vouru-kasha, and all earthly waters (standing, running, wells, springs, rain, canals), described as good waters created by Mazda. The text promises that anyone who sacrifices piously to the good waters with the best Zaothras will receive splendour, glory, health, bodily vigour, possessions, a legitimate heir, long life, and content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l17044-l17118","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    LVII.  299 / VIII. / YASNA    LVII.  305 / XIII.; lines 17044-17118","start":"17044","end":"17118","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"The passage contains a hymn in which the worshippers praise Sraosha (Obedience) as blessed, stately, and victorious over the whole earth, worshiping his gifts and saying his body is the Mathra. They extol his martial power as a warrior armed with shielding armour, skull‑cleaver of the Daevas, and holy conqueror whose victorious powers and Ascendency, along with that of Arrti, are worshiped. Every house guarded by Sraosha, where he is befriended and welcomed and where a holy man advances in holy thoughts and righteous words and deeds, is also venerated. The speaker vows to worship Sraosha with the Yasna of the Yazads, together with consecrated waters, Blessedness, and Nairya‑sangha, asking that he come to aid them. The introduction to Yasna LVIII then presents their service or worship as a defence and shield offered to increase homage and praise of God; Blessedness and Piety accompany it, its results are a well‑thought thought, a word well spoken, and a deed well done, and it is asked to shelter them from the Daeva and the evil‑minded man.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The speakers declare that they worship Sraosha (Obedience).","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Sraosha is described as blessed, stately, and as one who smites with victory both here and not here, and on the entire earth.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The worshippers say they worship all the gifts of Sraosha, whose body is identified as the Mathra.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Sraosha’s body is said to be the Mathra (a sacred utterance or formula).","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Sraosha’s gifts are described as martial: he is armed with shielding armour and is a warrior strong of hand.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Sraosha is called the skull‑cleaver of the Daevas and the holy conqueror of the conqueror.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Sraosha possesses victorious powers and an Ascendency which is worshipped.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The Ascendency of Sraosha is said to conquer that of others, and the Ascendency of Arrti is also praised.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:9","text

content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l17925-l18008","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    LXV.  319 / YASNA    LXVIII.  321 / YASNA    LXVIII.  323 / YASNA    LXX.  325; lines 17925-18008","start":"17925","end":"18008","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"The speaker, representing the worshipping community, offers sacrificial worship to the Bountiful Immortals, especially Ahura Mazda as Creator and helper, and also honors Zarathustra as chieftain of the rite. He proclaims the divinely established institutions associated with Ahura Mazda, the Good Mind, Righteousness, the desired Realm, Piety, Weal and Immortality, the body and soul of the Kine, Ahura Mazda’s Fire, Sraosha, Rashnu, Mithra, the holy Wind, the Mazdayasnian Religion, and various protective prayers. These are declared so that the worshippers may attain true zealous speech, become prophets, aid the one who proclaims Mazda, be friends and useful servants of Ahura Mazda, and live as holy men who think, speak, and do good. They pray that Ahura Mazda may approach them with the Good Mind and that their souls may advance in good. Finally, they praise the flood and ebb and roar of the good waters and the royal, glittering Apam Napat with fleet horses, for the sake of sacrifice and praise of all holy creation, and they invoke and sacrifice to Sraosha, Obedience the blessed.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The speaker states that he would worship the Bountiful Immortals with his sacrifice, describing them as those who rule and dispose all things aright.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The speaker approaches Ahura Mazda with praise and worships him in sacrifice.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Ahura Mazda is described as a deity and lord, the Creator, a gracious helper, and the maker of all good things.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Zarathustra Spitama is worshipped in the sacrifice and is called the chieftain of the rite.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The speaker declares institutions established for the community, emphasizing that they are exact and undeviating.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The institutions declared include those of Ahura Mazda, the Good Mind, Asha Vahishta (Righteousness the Best), Khshathra-vairya (the Realm to be desired), Aramaiti (Piety within), and those of Weal and Immortality.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Other institutions mentioned pertain to the body of the Kine, the Kine’s soul, Ahura Mazda’s Fire, Sraosha, Rashnu, Mithra of the wide pastures, the good and holy Wind, the Mazdayasnian Religion, and several forms of prayer.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Certain prayers are described as good and pious: a prayer for blessings, a prayer that frees one from belying, and a prayer content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l19787-l19909","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"VISPARAD    XII.  353 / VISPARAD    XIII.  355 / VISPARAD    XXIII.  363 / AFRINAGAN.; lines 19787-19909","start":"19787","end":"19909","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"“Live thou long and blessed be thou … and I pray for Heaven (for thee) the best world of the saints, shining, all glorious.”","summary":"The passage gives ritual instructions that if a disciple fails to present specified Myazda offerings at certain observances, the Ratu who guides him must expel him from the Mazdayasnian community and impose expiatory deeds, while emphasizing “Righteousness the Best” as a blessing. It then offers a blessing for royal province-chiefs, asking Ahura Mazda to grant them strength, victory over malicious and godless foes, steadfastness in religious thought, word, and deed, good repute, and a far‑seeing soul, along with long life for the aid of holy men, the crushing of evil, and entry into Heaven, the shining best world of the saints. The blessing further invokes sacrifice and homage for personified day‑lords, month‑lords, year‑lords, lords of the seasons, and a lofty lord who is the Righteous Ritual itself, together with lords of the ritual associated with specific seasonal times. The Afrin Gatha portion affirms that, just as the Ahu is to be chosen, so is the Ratu from the Righteous Order, described as a creator of mental goodness and right actions for Ahura, that the Kingdom belongs to Mazda who can provide a nurturer to the poor, and it includes a confession of Mazda‑worship in praise of Ahura Mazda and the Bountiful Immortals.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The text lists a third, fourth, fifth, and sixth Myazda, associated respectively with Paitiihiahya, Ayathrima, Maidhyairya, and Hamaspathmaedhaya.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"If a man does not give the third Myazda of Paitiihiahya, the Ratu who should receive it and has had the person under his guidance is instructed to expel that disciple as a reprobate from among the Mazdayasnians.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"If a man does not offer the fourth Myazda of Ayathrima, the Ratu who guides him is to expel that disciple as a “refuse beast” from the Mazdayasnians.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"If a man does not give the fifth Myazda of Maidhyairya, the Ratu to whom it belongs as a perquisite and who has the person under his guidance is to expel him as an alien from the Mazdayasnians.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"If a man does not give the sixth Myazda of Hamaspathmaedhaya, the Ratu responsible for that Myazda, who has the person under his discipline to teach him the lore of Ahura, is to expel him as ignorant from the Mazdayasnians.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The Ratu is described as having disciples under his guidance or discipline in order to teach them the lore of Ahura.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"After expelling the delinquent disciple, the Ratu is instructed to decry him, drive him out, and lay expiating deeds upon him without reserve.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The disciple is warned to beware of failing to bring his Myazda and, if he fails, to bear what is due in accordance with the rules.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"“Righteousness (called) the Best” is described as a blessing and weal for a man when there is right orientation toward it.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The speaker blesses in prayer the royal province‑chiefs, described as faithful worshippers of Ahura Mazda, asking for increased strength, victory, influential rule, authoritative power, supportive help, long duration of their reign, prolonged bodily vitality, and health.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The blessing asks for strength that is well‑shaped, stately, Ahura‑made, crushing, and victorious, giving an ascendency that subdues those filled with furious hate and destroys deadly, godless foes.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"The prayer asks that the province‑governor conquer in victorious battles every malicious foe, including those profane in thought, word, and deed, and that he be unvarying in smiting every foe and every Daeva‑worshipper.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"The prayer asks that the province‑governor be well rewarded, of good repute, and possess a far‑foreseeing preparation of the soul.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"The blessing says to the addressee, “Live thou long and blessed be thou,” wishing that he live for the aid of holy men and the crushing of evil.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"The speaker prays for Heaven for the addressee, described as “the best world of the saints, shining, all glorious.”","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:16","text":"The speaker blesses in prayer the sacrifice, homage, and the strength and swiftness of day‑lords, lords of the days, month‑lords, year‑lords, and lords of the seasons in their course.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:17","text":"The blessing includes worship, homage, propitiation, and praise of a lofty lord identified as the Righteous Ritual itself, and of the greatest lords of the ritual at the time of Havani and at several named seasonal observances (Maidhyo‑zaremaya, Maidhyo‑shema, Paiti.mahya, Ayathrima, Maidhyairya, Hamaspathmaedhaya).","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:18","text":"The Afrin Gatha says that as the Ahu is to be chosen, so the Ratu from the Righteous Order is to be chosen, who is a creator of mental goodness and of actions of life done for Ahura, and that the Kingdom belongs to Mazda, who may offer a nurturer to the poor.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:19","text":"The speaker confesses himself a Mazda‑worshipper for the praise of Ahura Mazda, described as resplendent and glorious, and for the praise of the Bountiful Immortals.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Spitama Zarathustra","description":"Named addressee content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l18100-l18185","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    LXVIII.  323 / YASNA    LXX.  325 / YASNA    LXXI.  327 / YASNA    LXXI.  329; lines 18100-18185","start":"18100","end":"18185","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"This passage from Yasna LXXI describes a litany of sacrifices offered to the ritual fire that consumes sanctified wood, to waters, plants, trees, land, heaven, stars, moon, sun, lights, various animals, female and male creatures, mountains, lakes, fires, and truthful words. Ahura Mazda is hailed as the skilful maker who has created many good things, including lakes and creatures made suitable for sacrifice through Asha Vahishta (Righteousness the Best). Truthful words and the Gathas (holy hymns ruling in the ritual order) are invoked and worshiped for protection, shielding, guarding, watching, and as preparation for the soul. The worshipers also sacrifice to Weal (complete welfare), Deathlessness (immortal being of the good), the question of the Lord and His lore (holy chiefs), and the heroic Haptanghaiti, holy lord of the ritual order. A voice (identified in the note as Ahura speaking) instructs holy Zarathustra to seek a friend and protector who is holy beyond the holy and truer than the true, declaring that a person is evil if they are best to the evil and holy if the holy is their friend. These are called the best words which Ahura Mazda spoke to Zarathustra. Ahura Mazda then commands Zarathustra to pronounce these words at the last ending of his life, promising that if he does so, Ahura will keep his soul far away from Hell, as distant as the breadth and extension of the earth. Finally, the text states that as the holy one desires, so he shall be, and that he will cause his soul to pass over.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"A fire is described as cutting, sucking out, and consuming dry wood which has been sanctified and carefully selected.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The speaker declares that they sacrifice to the strength, victory, glory, and speed of certain words as these words go forth for their work.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The speaker lists all springs of water, water-streams, growing plants, forest-trees, the entire land and heaven, all the stars, the moon and sun, and all lights without beginning to their course as recipients of sacrifice.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The speaker sacrifices to all cattle, aquatic beasts, beasts that live on land, beasts that strike the wine, beasts that roam the plains, and those of cloven hoof.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The speaker sacrifices to all good and holy female creatures in the creation and addresses Ahura Mazda as the skilful maker who has made many good things in the world.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The speaker sacrifices to male creatures in the creation that belong to Ahura Mazda and are described as meet for sacrifice because of Asha Vahishta (Righteousness the Best).","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The speaker sacrifices to all mountains described as brilliant with holiness, to all lakes which Mazda created, and to all fires.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The speaker sacrifices to all truthful and correctly spoken words, described as having both rewards and Piety within them, and worships them for protection, shielding, guarding, watching, and preparation.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"The speaker says they worship these entities for protection and shielding, for guarding and watching, and asks that they be for preparation.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The speaker calls upon the Gathas, described as bountiful holy ones ruling in the ritual order, and sacrifices to them for protection and shielding, for guarding and watching, and asks that they be a preparation for him.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The speaker explicitly states that he calls on the Gathas for his own soul and would worship them for protection, shielding, guarding, and watching.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"The speaker sacrifices to Weal (complete welfare), described as holy and ruling in its course in the ritual order, and to Deathlessness (the immortal being of the good), also described as holy and ruling in the ritual order.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"The speaker sacrifices to the question of the Lord, to His lore termed the holy chiefs, and to the heroic Haptanghaiti, described as the holy lord of the ritual order.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"A voice (marked by the translator as possibly Frasha or Ahura speaking) says that the holy Zarathustra should seek out a friend and a protector.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"The same voice tells Zarathustra to make for himself a friend who is holy beyond the holy and truer than the true, and states that this is the better thing.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:16","text":"The voice declares that \"he is evil who is the best to the evil\" and \"he is holy to whom the holy is a friend,\" and says that these are the best of words, those which Ahura Mazda spoke to Zarathustra.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:17","text":"Ahura Mazda instructs Zarathustra to pronounce these words at the last ending of his life.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:18","text":"Ahura Mazda promises that if Zarathustra pronounces these words at the last ending of his life, He will keep Zarathustra's soul away from Hell, as far away as the breadth and extension of the earth.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:19","text":"A following statement addresses the holy one and asserts that as he desires, so shall he be, and that he shall cause his soul to pass over.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Ahura Mazda","description":"Divine being addressed as the skilful maker who has made many good things, including lakes and creatures, and who speaks \"best words\" to Zarathustra and promises to keep his soul away from Hell.","role_refs":["role:1","role:2","role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:4","ev:5","ev:8","ev:9"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Zarathustra","description":"Holy person addressed directly in the passage, instructed to seek a friend and protector, to make a friend holy beyond the holy and truer than the true, and to pronounce certain words at the last ending of his life so that his soul Ahura is declared the awarder of highest good and deepest evil and is invoked to grant the 'eternal two' rewarding Immortals through inspired teachings. The speaker will proclaim the teachings' threats and promises, asks for a sign or instrument from the holy Fire to settle disputes with a forged blade of justice, and denounces a murderous opponent as a son of the Lie and of Akoman's seed while challenging the devotion of chieftains. A temptation of Zarathustra is noted, with a parallel in the Vendidad; his example encourages the righteous soul to become a conqueror, contrasted with Karpans and a typical destroyer who would ruin the world and bring creatures to Hell, while true disciples are promised recompense. Saving knowledge called Kisti, conceived by Mazda in sacred verse, is said to be acquired by a king, preserved in the memory of faithful priests under his rule, and embodied by a female saint. In an assembly the speaker notices devoted friends and declares that Archangels are of one mind with Mazda in bestowing spiritual blessings, chiefly inspired words that discipline and guide hope. He prays for these blessings for Ahura's elect, affirms that Ahura knows and favors the man who obeys commands and believes doctrines, and expresses a desire to approach the Bountiful Immortals with full appreciation of their sacred names. Finally, addressing assembled throngs, it warns them not to listen to Mathra or the sinner whose commands would bring home, village, region, and province to ruin and death, and urges them instead to content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l8815-l8918","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    XLV.  129 / YASNA    XLVI.  I3I / I32  THE    GAT  HAS. / YASNA    XLVI.  13; lines 8815-8918","start":"8815","end":"8918","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Commentary and translation on Yasna XLVI discuss a narrow path leading to eternal Hell for the faithless but state that their destruction is not yet decided and that even hostile groups may be blessed if they repent. A converted tribe (Fryana) provides pious proselytes who aid the righteous order, with God dwelling among them. Zarathustra rhetorically offers spiritual life from Ahura and future temporal wealth as rewards to princes and followers who support his cause, calls them good helpers of the tribes, and shifts attention from a single heroic king (Vutaspa) to all those whom Ahura will recognize in His assembly. He addresses his family, the Spitamas, and allies such as Frashao^tra and the Hvogvas, exhorting them to righteousness and promising a sacred scene where Immortals dwell with God and the faithful sing praises in true metres; Ahura, who infallibly discerns truth, will heed and answer obedient men who offer to the cause. He again holds out spiritual rewards and threatens oppressing clans with commensurate visitation, stressing that his promises and threats follow Ahura's will, and closes by emphasizing reward for everyone who aids his great affair, asserting divine inspiration. The accompanying translation shows Zoroaster lamenting lack of support from kin, peers, and workers, wondering to what land he should turn, while a footnote interprets this as seeking a land where his rejected religion may be established and where he may go with his praises of the true God.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"A narrow path is described that becomes narrow to the faithless, from which they fall into eternal Hell.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The destruction of those who might fall from the path is said not to be yet decided, and there is hope for tribesmen of Ahura, pagans, aliens, and even Turanian enemies.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Even Turanian enemies may be blessed if they repent, and some of them have already turned.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The converted tribe Fryana is said to have offered many pious proselytes.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"These proselytes help advance the righteous order together with the holy people, and God dwells with them.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Zaratluutra, referring to himself rhetorically or through another speaker, offers a reward to any prince who will join his cause with retainers.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The prince is urged not to be deterred by prior refusals or by the small numbers of Zarathustra\u0019s bands.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The promised reward is spiritual life from Ahura for every faithful follower together with future temporal wealth.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Zaratluutra declares that such a recruit will be a \u001cgood mate\u001d in service and the first helper of the tribes.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"A question is posed asking who is the friend and powerful coadjutor offered this reward and service.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Zaratluutra identifies the king Vutaspa as that friend and coadjutor.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Zaratluutra seeks to divert his hearers from a pernicious trust in individuals, even if the individual is heroic.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"He implies that he appeals not to one man only but to all whom Ahura will recognize in His assembly through the inspired suffrage of the mass.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"Zaratluutra addresses a group composed chiefly of his family, the Spitamas.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"The Spitamas are implied to be enlightened in sacred lore and among the foremost of the Ar(e)dra.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:16","text":"Zaratluutra calls on Frashao^tra together with the Hvogvas, exhorting them to continue in their righteous course.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:17","text":"They are encouraged to act in harmony with those whom they desire as Saviours for the land.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:18","text":"Zaratluutra assures them they will reach a sacred scene where the Immortals dwell with God.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:19","text":"The sacred scene is further described as a place where the faithful sing their praises in perfection using true metres.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:20","text":"Ahura is said to infallibly discern truth and to heed and answer the praises sung there.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:21","text":"The praises at that scene are those of obedient men who offer themselves to the cause.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:22","text":"Zaratluutra again presents spiritual rewards as the best gifts of inspired revelation.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:23","text":"He threatens commensurate visitation upon oppressing clans.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:24","text":"He states that his promises and threats are in harmony with Ahura\u0019s will, which has guided his statements.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:25","text":"After complaints, threats, and stern injunctions, he closes with the repeated word \u001creward\u001d for every man who will aid his great affair.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:26","text":"He appeals to God Himself, asserting divine inspiration for all that he has said.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:27","text":"In the translation, Zoroaster asks to what land he should turn and whither he should go.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:28","text":"He laments that no kinsman prince or allied peer gives offerings to help his cause.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:29","text":"He adds that neither the throngs of labour nor even such as these, nor still less the evil, support him.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:30","text":"A footnote explains the line as Zoroaster asking in what land he shall establish his religion, since it is rejected where he is.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:31","text":"The same note glosses his question as asking whither he shall go with his praises of the true God.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:32","text":"Another footnote remarks that certain figures (the /^aetu, airyaman, and verezmem) are elsewhere alluded to as belonging to a hostile party and therefore not among those from whom the prophet would be expelled.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Ahura {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l6194-l6285","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    XXXIII.  77 / YASNA    XXXIII.  79 / YASNA    XXXIV. / YASNA    XXXIV.  8  I; lines 6194-6285","start":"6194","end":"6285","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Translator-commentator prose describing Ahura's caring Kingdom contrasted with the Daevas' religion, the composer-prophet's doubt and prayer for a confirming sign, the checking and spiritual punishment of persecuting enemies, the departure of personified Good Intention and Piety from sinners, divine favor that grants the faithful spiritual Deathlessness and welfare, a plea for guidance in worship and error-free religious paths, the revealed way of the Saoshyawts where Ahura dwells and rewards the well-doer, the Kine as symbol of holy settlements and support, earthly life as vestibule to heavenly life, and the assertion that deeds of Piety and the Saoshyawts' words and actions themselves constitute the highest wisdom and the saving \"way.\"","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The divine Kingdom is described as caring for the righteous poor and as irreconcilably distinct from the Daevas and their polluted followers, being beyond and before them in the spirit of its reign.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The composer is acutely aware of the sharp difference between this Kingdom and the rival religion and adds an interdict marking this separation.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The composer expresses a serious doubt, asking whether it is really true that the deities are with the Righteous Order and the Good Mind, the God who looks on the goodness of the heart and the activity of the hands, and he asks for a sign so he may persevere in homage while life lasts.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"He notes that the struggle with opponents, though showing signs of a favorable outcome, is far from over, which explains his misgivings.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"He longs for the ar(e)dra, men who through experience of the grace of God could help turn sorrow into blessing by firmly establishing the holy religious system with enlarged understanding.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Feeling he has no helper other than the deities, the composer resolves to wait for the ar(e)dra and asks the deities to save them by their already offered means of grace.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"He regards it as a sign already given that the enemy are checked and cowed for the moment, though not fully repelled; these enemies had previously held the upper hand, caused many deaths, and whose ruler persecuted holy vows.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The enemies are now struck with terror by the action taken by the faithful, and their chief retribution is viewed as spiritual: because they will not encourage righteous Order and righteous intentions, the personified Good Intention, grieved, will depart from them.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"The composer declares that sinners who desert the kindly and sacred Piety and lack experience of the Good Mind will be similarly deserted: the characteristics of righteousness will avoid them as unclean creatures flee from humans.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"He interprets this desertion and spiritual retribution as a sign or result declared by the All-wise to steady his wavering soul and as proofs of divine favor that terrify the enemies and advance the faithful, giving them righteous eminence in the divine Kingdom.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Kindly Piety is said to increase for the faithful two comprehensive blessings: spiritual Deathlessness, begun in anticipation here, and its necessary condition, Welfare; these blessings are to be increased as food for Mazda's straitened people, or better, to His glory as their monarch, and by their means Ahura may defend Himself from persecuting idolatrous foes.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Considering the importance of correct understanding in religious and political duties, the composer fervently prays to be guided in establishing ceremonial and praises, asking Mazda to declare the kind of worship that may secure the ashis, the blessed rewards, and to teach religious paths of the Good Mind about which no error is possible.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"He answers that the way which Ahura has revealed as the Good Mind's own consists of the revealed precepts of the Saoshyawts, and that in these paths where Ahura dwells the well-doer may prosper from devotion to religious truths and gain an immediate reward from the hand of God.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"Recalling the original calamity and woes of the Kine, he declares this way to be the one to be chosen for earthly life as the vestibule to the heavenly one; those who toil for the Kine, which here represents the holy settlements and their chief source of riches and support, strive to further and demonstrate the wisdom of that way by every righteous contrivance.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"He asserts that the deeds of Piety are themselves the highest wisdom and that the words and righteous actions of the Saoshyawts not only declare and make but actually constitute \"the way.\"","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Composer-prophet","description":"The speaker or composer who reflects on the divine Kingdom, experiences doubt, prays for a sign and guidance, and interprets events as signs of divine favor and retribution.","role_refs":["role:1"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:3","ev:6","ev:8","ev:9","ev:10"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Ahura / Mazda / the All-wise God","description":"The supreme deity addressed as ruler whose Kingdom cares for the righteous poor, who allies with Righteous Order and Good Mind, gives signs, declares results, grants spiritual Deathlessness and Welfare, dwells in the paths of truth, rewards the well-doer, and defends Himself and His people from persecuting foes.","role_refs":["role:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:2","ev:6","ev:7","ev:8","ev:9"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Daevas and their polluted followers","description":"Rival divine beings and their followers associated with an opposing religion, contrasted sharply with Ahura's Kingdom and declared irreconcilably distinct from it.","role_refs":["role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Enemies and persecuting idolatrous foe","description":"Human opponents who formerly had the upper hand, caused many deaths, persecuted holy vows, and now are checked, cowed, and subject to spiritual retribution; also described as persecuting and idolatrous foes.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:4","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"Ar(e)dra men who could help","description":"Men longed for by the composer who, from experience of God's grace, could help turn sorrow into blessing by firmly establishing the holy religious system with enlarged understanding.","role_refs":["role:5"],"evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:6","name_or_label":"Righteous Order","description":"A personified religious or cosmic order with whom the deities are said to be, and which the enemies refuse to encourage.","role_refs":["role:6"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:4"]},{"id":"fig:7","name_or_label":"Good Mind","description":"A personified divine mental or moral faculty allied with Ahura, whose paths are errorless and whose experience the sinners lack.","role_refs":["role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:5","ev:8","ev:9"]},{"id":"fig:8","name_or_label":"Good Intention","description":"A personified righteous intention that, grieved, departs from the enemies when they refuse righteous Order and intentions.","role_refs":["role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"fig:9","name_or_label":"Kindly sacred Piety","description":"A personified kindly and sacred Piety that sinners desert and that in turn increases blessings such as spiritual Deathlessness and Welfare for the faithful.","role_refs":["role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:5","ev:7","ev:10"]},{"id":"fig:10","name_or_label":"Righteousness / characteristics of righteousness","description":"Personified righteous qualities which avoid sinners, likened to unclean creatures fleeing from humans.","role_refs":["role:6"],"evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:11","name_or_label":"Saoshyawts","description":"Revealed savior-like figures whose precepts constitute the Good Mind's way and whose words and righteous actions declare, make, and constitute the saving path.","role_refs":["role:8"],"evidence_refs":["ev:9","ev:10"]},{"id":"fig:12","name_or_label":"The Kine","description":"The Kine, which here represents the holy settlements and their chief source of riches and support, for which people toil as part of the chosen way of life.","role_refs":["role:9"],"evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"fig:13","name_or_label":"Mazda's straitened people","description":"The oppressed people belonging to Mazda who receive increased blessings like spiritual Deathlessness and Welfare as food or support.","role_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:14","name_or_label":"Unfortunate sinners","description":"Those who desert kindly and sacred Piety and have no experience of the Good Mind, and who suffer desertion by righteousness.","role_refs":[],"evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:15","name_or_label":"Unclean creatures","description":"Creatures described as fleeing from humans, used as a simile for how righteousness avoids Every man of Piety is a wise citizen aligned with the holy Order, and all who are truly within Mazda's realm share this status. content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l12683-l12717","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    II.  205 / YASNA    III.  207 / YASNA  III. / YASNA    III.  209; lines 12683-12717","start":"12683","end":"12717","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"\"And I desire to approach both Haoma and the Haoma-juice with a Yasht ... I will confess myself a Mazdayasnian, of Zarathustra's order, a foe to the Daevas ... for sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise.\"","summary":"A first-person liturgical speaker declares the desire to approach Haoma, its juice, wood-billets, and perfume with ritual hymns (Ya^t/Ya5t) to propitiate the Fravashi of Zarathustra and the Fire, described as Ahura Mazda's son and a Yazad. The speaker similarly approaches the mighty Fravashis of saints, of those who kept the ancient lore, and of kin, as well as all lords of the ritual order and good Yazads, heavenly and earthly, associated with Righteousness (Asha Vahrrta). He names Ahura Mazda’s Righteous Order and Best Mind as his true helpers. A guardian is imagined seeking a joy-creating Kine, described as the living symbol of peace, and the speaker prays for lands that live in justice under the splendours of the sun, to be gained as righteous conquests. The passage then portrays a heroic settler and valiant citizen who, under Ahura Mazda’s Sovereign Authority and prosperity, can grant this living sign and make the last imperilled farm flourish near fields held by a foeman.
