{"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l13084-l13151","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    IV.  215 / YASNA    IV.  217 / YASNA   VI.  2  19 / YASNA    VI.  22  1; lines 13084-13151","start":"13084","end":"13151","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"A litany enumerates many objects of worship honored \"with our sacrifice\": the Mathra Spenta (holy word), Zarathustrian law, and Mazdayasnian religion; a sacred Mazda-made mountain and all holy mountains; kingly glory, sanctity, glory, benefit, blessing, the pious saint, and a mighty curse of wisdom; waters, lands, plants, places and their springs, with Ahura Mazda as lord of the district; lords of day, month, and year; the divine beings Haurvatat, Ameretat, and Sraosha; Haoma and its juice; the Fravashi of Zarathustra and of all saints; ritual materials like wood and perfume; the Fire, son of Ahura Mazda; all Yazads and lords of the ritual order at their proper times. It closes with a brief dialogue rubric between the Ratu and the Zaotar assigning speech in the ritual.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The worshippers honor the Mathra Spenta with their sacrifice, describing it as glorious and true, and as the Zarathustrian law revealed against the Daevas.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The Zarathustrian law and its long descent, together with the good Mazdayasnian religion, are explicitly worshipped with sacrifice.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Mount Ushi-darena is called Mazda-made, a glorious Yazad, and shining with holiness, and is worshipped.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"All mountains that shine with holiness and abundant brilliance are described as Mazda-made and as holy lords of the ritual order, and they are worshipped.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The \"mighty Kingly glory\" is described as Mazda-made, mighty, unconsumed, and delivering men with its inherent power, and is worshipped along with good Sanctity, Glory, and Benefit.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Sanctity is characterized as brilliant, lofty, powerful, and stately, and associated with delivering men.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"A pious and good Blessing, the pious man or saint, and a Yazad named the mighty Curse of wisdom are worshipped.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Waters, lands, plants, places, districts, pastures, abodes, and their springs of water are all worshipped with sacrifice.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"The lord of the district is identified as Ahura Mazda Himself and is worshipped with sacrifice.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The greatest lords associated with time—Day-lords in the day’s duration and daylight, Month-lords, and Year-lords—are worshipped.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Haurvatat is said to guard the water, and Ameretat to guard the plants and the wood; both, along with Sraosha, are worshipped.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Sraosha is described as blessed, stately, smiting with the blow of victory, making settlements advance, and as a holy lord of the ritual order, and is worshipped.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"Haoma and the Haoma-juice are worshipped with sacrifice, and the sacred Fravashi of Zarathustra Spitama the saint is also worshipped.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"Wood-billets and perfume are worshipped, as is the Fire, described as Ahura Mazda’s son and as a holy lord of the ritual order.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"The good, heroic, bountiful Fravashis of the saints are worshipped.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:16","text":"All the holy Yazads and all the lords of the ritual order are worshipped at the time of Havani, Savanghi, and all the greatest lords at their proper times, followed by the recitation YeNhe hatam.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:17","text":"In a rubric marked \"The Ratu,\" the line states IO9 / I  IO  THE    GATHAS.; lines 7663-7708","start":"7663","end":"7708","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"A devoted speaker, filled with hatred for opposing gods, surveys the assembled masses and addresses Ahura while really speaking to the people. He asks who among them is the righteous believer or the sceptic, and which man is governed by Angra Mainyu or as evil as a certain sinful chief who opposes him as Angra once opposed Ahura. He laments that this chief is still tolerated. He then protests having to endure opponents who present their Lie-demon as a Goddess and asks how he can drive this female figure to Hell, not to hesitant onlookers but to those already disobedient and cut off from the community, who have not shared the counsels of the Good Mind. He envisions delivering this Lying Goddess, in the persons of her adherents, to the Holy Order embodied in saints so that she may be slain with the snaithu and destroyed as falsehood by the Mathras of Ahura’s doctrine, moving from mere endurance of wicked corrupters and silent or complicit masses toward spreading slaughter and their total overthrow. He then turns to an approaching collision between hosts that claim an urvata (pledge) and prays to know to which host Ahura will give the prize. He asks who will be the champion (verethrem-van) to lead the victors, taking up both the snaithu and the Mathra to contend for “both the worlds,” and desires that this champion, like Zarathustra previously, be approached by obedient wills and moved to holy work by the inspiring Good Mind.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The speaker is described as devoted to his cause, filled with hatred in his spirit toward opposing Gods, casting a searching glance over the masses divided into groups each headed by a chief, and addressing Ahura formally while really speaking to the people.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The speaker asks Ahura who among those present is the righteous The Offering takes place,” indicating that the following verses describe the offering segment of the ritual.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"“Good thoughts, good words, and good deeds” are listed among the things that “we offer” and “make known with celebrations.”","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Haomas, meat-offerings (Myazdas), Zaothras, a Baresman spread with sanctity, flesh, Haoma and Haoma-juice, wood-billets, and their perfume are enumerated as items included in the offerings.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Within the list of offerings, two beings are named with glosses: Haurvatat is described as “who guards the water,” and Ameretat as “who guards the plants and wood.”","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The offerings also encompass “this sacred lordship and chieftainship,” the timely prayer with blessing, the heard recital of the Gathas, and the well-said Mathras, which are said to be offered and made known with celebrations.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The practitioners state that they announce these offerings with celebrations and present them to Ahura Mazda, content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l16896-l17022","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    LV.  295 / YASNA    LVII.  297 / YASNA    LVII.  299 / VIII.; lines 16896-17022","start":"16896","end":"17022","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"\"We worship Sraosha (Obedience) the blessed...\"","summary":"This passage consists of several liturgical sections praising Sraosha (\"Obedience\"). It recalls that Haoma worshipped Sraosha on the highest height of Haraiti and describes Sraosha as understanding, intoning hymns, revealing the sacred word, and having first place in the Mathra. Sraosha’s thousand-pillared house, self-lighted and star-studded, stands on high Haraiti and receives key liturgical compositions such as Ahuna-vairya (called the axe of victory), Haptanghaiti, Fshusho-mathra, and all Yasna sections. By Sraosha’s might the Bountiful Immortals descend upon the earth of seven quarters; he is portrayed as teacher of the law who strides across the earth among embodied dwellers. The Religion confesses Ahura Mazda, Good Mind, Righteousness the Best, Khshathra-vairya, Piety the Bounteous, Universal Weal, and Immortality, and questions are asked to the Lord while Mazda’s lore is written. Worshippers implore Sraosha to protect their lives in both the corporeal world and the world of mind against unhappy death, demonic Wrath and Vidhatu, and hostile hosts with bloody spears, asking for swiftness for their teams, bodily soundness, insight into foes, and their sudden death. Finally, Sraosha is depicted as being drawn by four white, shining, gold-hoofed racers, faster than horses, winds, rain, clouds, birds, or arrows. These racers obey mental commands, overtake all others yet are never overtaken, avoid weapons on both sides, and carry Obedience the blessed as he travels from India in the East to the West.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Sraosha is worshipped and addressed as \"the Haraiti.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Haoma is described as a reviver and healer, beautiful, kingly, and of the golden eye.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Sraosha intones hymns on every side.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Sraosha possesses understanding, brilliant form, many explanations and revelations of the word, and has the first place in the Mathra.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Sraosha’s house stands with a thousand pillars on the highest height of high Haraiti, self-lighted from within and star-studded from without.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Ahuna-vairya (called the axe of victory), Haptanghaiti, Fshusho-mathra (which smites with victory), and all the Yasna sections come to Sraosha.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"By Sraosha’s might, victorious power, wise conduct, and knowledge, the Bountiful Immortals descend upon The speaker prays for sanctity, the strength of the holy man, and Ahura's lore to be present in a house, invoking the good, heroic, and bountiful Fravashis of the saints to come hand in hand with the worshippers, bringing healing gifts as extensive as earth, rivers, and sun to assist the righteous, hinder the hostile, and increase riches and glory. Sraosha (Obedience) is asked to conquer disobedience, and a series of moral virtues are invoked to triumph over their opposing vices, culminating in Righteous Order gaining victory over the Demon of the Lie. The Bountiful Immortals, governed in the house by Sraosha, are described as seeking good Yasnas, praises, and one good sacrifice and act of homage, a good offering for salvation and praise, together with a long continued offering of the entire self. The prayer further asks that their brilliant glory, bright abundance, legitimate offspring, and long companionship—supporting blessedness that teaches concerning glory—never desert the house. Another section asks that minds, souls, and bodies be glorified, that bodies may go openly to heaven, the best world of the saints devoted to Ahura, accompanied by Asha Vahishta (Righteousness the Best), so that worshippers may see Ahura, approach and encircle him, attain complete companionship with him, and sacrifice to the Righteous Order, described as a bounteous Immortal. Yasna LXI then calls on the community to peal forth the Ahuna-vairya and send forth Asha Vahishta and the Yenghe hatam in liturgy \"between the heaven and earth,\" sending a pious prayer of the pious man for blessings and for the encounter with and displacement of Angra Mainyu and his likewise evil, death-bearing creatures, and for the dislodgment of the Kakharedhas, male and content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l2414-l2520","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"THE   GATHAS. / YASNA    XXIX. / THE   GATHAS. / YASNA    XXIX.; lines 2414-2520","start":"2414","end":"2520","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"In this portion of Yasna XXIX, the herds (or their guardians) question personified Righteousness (Asha) about how a guardian for the Kine (cow) was appointed, seeking a skilled and energetic cattle-chief who could protect her pasture and repel the fury of the wicked. Righteousness replies that they were perplexed and unable to obtain such a chieftain, emphasizing that beings like themselves cannot know the influences that approach and move the lofty fires which reveal the favour and will of God. A mightiest being is described, to whom those who have performed their actions approach with invocations and who has no need to ask. Zarathustra then intervenes and teaches that the Great Creator, Ahura Mazda, is most mindful of indications fulfilled in the deeds of demon-gods (Daevas) and men, past and future, and that Ahura is the discerning arbiter whose will determines what shall happen to humans. The speaker adds that his own soul and the soul of the mother Kine are making supplication to this Creator.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The herds ask Righteousness how her guardian for the Kine was appointed and how she secured for the Kine a skilled and energetic cattle-chief to protect her and her pasture from the fury of the wicked.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Righteousness (Asha) answers that they were in great perplexity and could not obtain a chieftain who was capable of smiting back the fury of the wicked and was himself without hate.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Righteousness states that beings such as they cannot know the influences that approach and move the lofty fires which reveal God.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"A being is described as the mightiest of beings, to whom those who have performed their actions approach with invocations.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"It is said of this mightiest being that he has no need to ask.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Zarathustra is explicitly mentioned as intervening in the discourse.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"The Great Creator is described as most mindful of uttered indications fulfilled in the deeds of demon-gods and men in Editorial notes explain that the Chinvat Bridge is the last crisis before salvation or perdition where souls of the good and evil meet their consciences, which encourage or revile them, and that the bridge expands for the pious. The speaker declares that Ahura’s adoration rules and is complete, that he yokes Ahura’s mighty ones, Holy Order, and Good Mind to help him. He approaches Ahura Mazda through the highest worship, using the sacred metric feet of Zarathustra and his peers, with hands outstretched in supplicating prayer, in union with ritual Truth, as a freely-giving helper endowed with the virtue of Good Mind. He further approaches Ahura and personified Righteousness with Yasnas of sacrifice, praising in response to divine mercies and relying on the holy actions of Good Mind within them, wishing to be like the wise man who as a supplicant gains his ends. content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l5695-l5796","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    XXXII.  67 / F   2 / YASNA    XXXIII.  69 / YASNA    XXXIII.  71; lines 5695-5796","start":"5695","end":"5796","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"He prays that an influence like that of the 'eternal two' might bear their spirit to the shining home of Paradise, it having attained to perfection by the help of the Best Mind of God within it.","summary":"Translator’s commentary and Gathic verses describe Zarathustra as a spiritual chieftain who urges chiefs and masses to bring sacrificial gifts, seeks more than simple morality, and prays for two pious chiefs to reach Paradise through the influence of a divine pair and the Best Mind of God. He petitions Mazda and Ahura for all phases of life, for the flourishing of accountable individuals under Good Mind, Sovereignty, and Sacred Order, and for the ultimate blessed state (ujta). Personified virtues such as Piety, Righteous Order, Good Mind, and the divine Kingdom are invoked to listen, pardon, strengthen him, and reveal Gnosis—the Religion. A central desire is the Thrift-law and the Avesta of the Ratu/Saoshyant. The section culminates in a dedication of Zarathustra’s body, obedience, religious eminence, and the kingdom he has saved and blessed to God. In the translated verses, Zarathustra—besought by the Kine and named by the Lord—acts by the laws of the primeval world, doing just deeds toward the wicked, the righteous, and those with equal fraud and righteous works; a footnote links this to the later idea of an intermediate place between Heaven and Hell. Just vengeance against the wicked and admonition for others’ good are described as gifts offered to religious faith and conscience in the loving approval of Ahura Mazda.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Chiefs and thronging masses are called upon, and sacrificial gifts are urged to pour in for offering and worship.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The central figure is described as not resting at bare morality for the simple multitude and therefore asking vigorously for sacrifice and hymn.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"He encourages two pious chiefs whose souls go hand in hand.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"He prays that an influence like that of the 'eternal two' might bear the chiefs’ spirit to the shining home of Paradise, after it has attained perfection by the help of the Best Mind of God within it.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"He asks Mazda to grant in His love all the happy phases of life that have been or will ever be experienced.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"He prays that their bodies, as separate accountable individuals, might flourish in the graces of the Good Mind, Holy Sovereignty, and Sacred Order until they are blessed with ujta, the summum bonum.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"He prays Piety, the Righteous Order, the Good Mind of God within His people, and His kingdom to turn their mental ears, listen, and pardon.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"He specifies the Thrift-law and the Avesta of the Ratu or Saoshyant as the central object of desire and asks Ahura to arise to his help and give spiritual strength through Righteousness and the Good Mind.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"He asks not to see the person of God but His nature, and to comprehend what the Sovereignty of God implies with its blessed rewards.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"He asks of Piety, acquired and practised and speaking within him, to reveal the Gnosis or Insight that is the Religion.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Translator explains verse 14 as expressing a dedication of all that he is and has to God: his flesh, body, religious eminence, obedience in word and deed inspired by Righteousness, and the kingdom he has saved and blessed.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"In the translation, a spiritual chieftain, besought-for by the Kine and named as Zarathustra by the Lord, will act according to the laws of the primeval world.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"He will do deeds most just toward the wicked, toward the righteous, and toward one whose deeds of fraud and righteous deeds combine in equal measure.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"A footnote suggests that the description of someone whose sins and good works are equal may be the origin of the later hamestaga concept, the souls in an intermediate place between Heaven and Hell whose sins and good works balance.","category":"other","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"Verse 2 describes a person who does evil to the wicked by word, thought and plan, and laboring with both hands, or admonishes someone for his good; such persons are said to be offering a gift to their religious faith in the love and approving view of Ahura Mazda, offering to conscience.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:11"]},{"id":"obs:16","text":"A footnote explains that these persons hold fast to the holy cause, and their vehemence in vengeance does not negate The speaker then invokes Divine Righteousness and Piety to bestow a sacred blessing made up of the attainments of the Good Mind within the soul and to grant a shared wish from Vistaspa and the speaker, including the grace to hear Mazda’s benignant words with understanding. Commentary describes a time when all people are intelligent because they are pious, expresses desire to see the place of Ahura Mazda known through Srosh, and notes that the greatest of the sacred Mathras should be taught to those whose understanding is confused. Further notes explain the Good Mind as the Spirit of God both in the divine mind and in the human soul. The prayer continues by beseeching the best gift from Ahura Mazda, united in will with Divine Righteousness, for the heroic man Frashaoitra and for the speaker, to be granted for all the ages of the Good Mind, which is described as Heaven and linked with the millennial renovation and a final body that will benefit Frashaoitra’s disciples. Ahura Mazda is praised as creator, radiant, glorious, wisest, and the bounteous Spirit who made, fashioned, nourished, and protected humans and disposes minds aright through his Righteous Order and grace. The speaker then dedicates the Yasna to personified qualities such as Good Mind, Righteousness the Best, desired Sovereignty, and Piety the Bountiful, as well as to Universal Weal and Immortality, to the body of the Kine and the Kine's Soul, and to the Fire of Ahura Mazda, which is said to have made the most effort for human succor compared to the Bountiful Immortals. The litany continues with an announcement to the Asnya, day-lords of the ritual order, including Havani, Savanghi, and Visya, and then to Mithra of the wide pastures, described as having a thousand ears and myriad eyes, and to Raman Zioastra. Translator notes clarify metaphors about Ahura Mazda's \"body\" and the exalted status of Fire and the ritual content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l11621-l11667","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    LIII.  187 / THE  GATHA(A)  VAHI6TA  ISTIS  (VAHIS- / YASNA    LIII.  189 / I90  THE    GATHAS.; lines 11621-11667","start":"11621","end":"11667","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"“That best prayer has been answered, the prayer of Zarathustra Spitama, that Ahura Mazda might grant him boons which flow from the good Order, a life prospered for eternal duration, and also those who deceived him as the good Faith’s disciples in word and deed. And may Kavi Vistaspa, the Zarathustrian Spitama, and Frashao.stra offer propitiation to Mazda in thought, word, and deed.”","summary":"The passage states that Zarathustra’s foremost prayer has been answered by Ahura Mazda, who grants boons arising from the good Order: an eternally prospered life for Zarathustra and the transformation of his deceivers into disciples of the good Faith. It then invokes Kavi Vistaspa, the Zarathustrian Spitama, and Frashao.stra to offer propitiation to Mazda in thought, word, and deed. Translator’s notes discuss the possible implication that Zarathustra was already dead when his prayer was heard, emphasize the conversion of former deceivers, highlight non‑ritual sanctity linked with worship, and debate the identity of the ‘Zarathustrian Spitama’ as a potential family representative of Zarathustra.","language":"English","quote_policy":"quoted"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Zarathustra Spitama is said to have offered a “best prayer” to Ahura Mazda requesting boons that flow from the good Order.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The text declares that Zarathustra’s “best prayer has been answered,” implying a divine response to his petition.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The requested boons are described as flowing from the “good Order.”","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"One of the boons requested or granted is “a life that is prospered for eternal duration.”","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Another boon concerns “those who deceived” Zarathustra, who are to be granted to him as the good Faith’s disciples in word and deed.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"A Pahlavi-based note explains that even the deceiver is to be instructed in the word and deed of the good religion, reinforcing the idea of conversion of former opponents.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The passage calls on Kavi Vistaspa, the Zarathustrian Spitama, and Frashao.stra to offer propitiation to Mazda.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Their propitiation to Mazda is specified as occurring “in The Yašt is described as a composite of fragments and the English rendering as rhythmical and somewhat free. The liturgical section then begins: at the morning hour of Havani, Haoma appears in human form to Zarathustra as the prophet serves and sanctifies the sacred Fire and sings the Gathas. Zarathustra, struck by the visitor’s surpassing beauty and immortality, asks his identity. Haoma replies that he is Haoma, holy and driving death afar, and instructs Zarathustra to pray to him, prepare him for drinking, and praise him as other Saoshyants do. Zarathustra praises Haoma and asks which man first prepared Haoma for the corporeal world and what blessing he gained. Haoma answers that Vivanghvat was the first of men to prepare him, and that Vivanghvat’s blessedness was the birth of his son Yima the brilliant, sunlike and of many herds, whose authority made herds and people free from dying, plants and waters free from drought, and provided imperishable food for men. In Yima’s reign there was neither cold nor heat, age nor death, nor demon-made envy; father and son walked together like fifteen-year-olds in stature and form as long as Yima ruled. A note identifies Vivanghvat as fifth from the primordial ancestor Gaya Maretan, the \"Iranian Adam,\" and as counterpart of the Indian Vivasvat, father of Yama, Manu, and even some content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l14327-l14424","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    X.  243 / YASNA   XI. / YASNA    XL  245 / YASNA    XII.  247; lines 14327-14424","start":"14327","end":"14424","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"“I confess myself a Mazdayasnian of Zarathustra’s order… I drive the Daevas hence; I confess as a Mazda-worshipper… to Ahura Mazda… I attribute all things good, whose is the Kine, whose is Asha, whose are the stars.”","summary":"The passage contains a Mazdayasnian confession in which a first-person worshipper declares allegiance to Zarathustra’s order, praises and offers sacrifices (even the ‘flesh of my very body’) to the Bountiful Immortals, and praises Righteousness. The confessor drives away the Daevas, professes estrangement from them, and aligns with the lore of the Lord and the Bountiful Immortals. Ahura Mazda is described as the good, holy, resplendent, glorious deity to whom all good things are attributed, including the sacred Kine, Asha (righteous order), and the stars whose light clothes glorious beings. The worshipper chooses Piety, rejects robbery and violence against the sacred Kine, deplores drought that wastes Mazdayasnian villages, seeks to remove the idea of nomadic wandering and tent-dwelling from the community, and vows never to be a source of wasting or withering to Mazdayasnian villages, even at the cost of body or life. Editorial notes comment on the antiquity of the text and remark that Zarathustra, Kavi Vistaspa, Frashaoshtra, and Gamaspa are mentioned in the wider piece but are not treated as demi-gods.","language":"English","quote_policy":"quoted"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The speaker states, “I confess myself a Mazdayasnian of Zarathustra’s order.”","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The speaker celebrates and presents good thoughts, good words, and good deeds, and repudiates all evil thoughts, words, and deeds.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The speaker offers sacrifice and homage to the Bountiful Immortals with mind, words, deeds, and entire person, saying that He is said to have first spread the Baresman bundles for the Bountiful Immortals, and to have first chanted Zarathushtra’s five Gathas with their metres, commentary (Zand), and question–answer exchanges, for sacrifice and praise. Sraosha builds a mighty house for the poor, fights the demon Aeshema with a battle-axe after sunset, and casts him down. He is depicted as an energetic, swift, strong, daring hero who returns victorious from his battles and sits as a companion among the Bountiful Immortals. Obedience’s presence in a dwelling causes evil terrors to depart from house, village, tribe, and country, and a holy man who welcomes Obedience practices better thoughts, truthful ritual words, and holy deeds. Sraosha is further described as conqueror of Kayadha and Kaidhya, smiter of the Lie-demon of the Daevas (destroyer of the world), and as a sleepless, vigilant guardian and watchman over the migrations Its \"measures\" are identified as the good thought, the good word, and the good deed. Four classes of men—priest, charioteer/warrior, tiller of the ground, and artisan—accompany the religious man in his duty with correct thought, truthful word, and righteous action, giving attention to rulers, fulfilling religious laws, and thereby furthering settlements in righteousness. A hierarchy of chiefs is described (house-chief, village-chief, tribe-chief, chief of the province, and a governor titled Zarathartra) for general provinces, and a slightly different hierarchy (house-chief, village-chief, tribe-chief, and Zarathustra as fourth) for the Zarathustrian district. Further questions define the \"thought well thought\" as what the holy man thinks when he puts holy thought before all else, the \"word well spoken\" as the Mathra Spenta (the bounteous word of reason), and the \"deed well done\" as one performed with praises by creatures who place Righteousness above all things. Mazda is said to make a proclamation announcing a holy one who is both heavenly and mundane; Mazda himself is described as the best and ruling one, and the proclaimed coming figure is holy and best, a ruler who does not exercise wanton or despotic power. content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l17657-l17744","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    LXII.  313 / YASNA    LXII.  315 / YASNA    LXV.  317 / YASNA    LXV.  319; lines 17657-17744","start":"17657","end":"17744","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"“O ye waters, I beseech of you this favour … grant me likewise what is still greater than this all … Immortality and Welfare.”","summary":"The passage instructs Zarathustra to begin his petitions by praying to the waters and offering sanctified Zaothras to them. The prayer continues by requesting something greater than these blessings—Immortality and Welfare—from the Yazads and from Ahura Mazda, described as maker of the kine, plants, and waters, who is asked to grant these two eternal gifts through his Good Mind in the doctrine. A related section describes offering Zaothra, Haoma, flesh, and Hadhanaepata with sanctity to the Ahurian One for the propitiation of Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Sraosha, and the ritual Fire.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Zarathustra is instructed that he should first pray to the waters and then offer sanctified pastures, stately Sraosha, Rashnu the most just, Fire as Ahura Mazda's son, royal Apam‑napat of the fleet horses, and all Yazads as holy bestowers of better gifts.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Holy waters and lands are explicitly asked to grant the requested wealth and offspring.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The petitioner asks the Yazads, described as holy, ruling mightily, and powerful, to grant something greater and more precious than wealth and offspring, namely Immortality and Welfare, and to grant it speedily according to a Gathic word about grace promoting weal.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"A further formula addresses Ahura Mazda, called maker of the kine, plants, and waters and the most bounteous Spirit, asking Editorial notes explain that Visparad means \"all the chiefs\" and that these lords function as ruling genii over their classes.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The speaker repeatedly says \"I announce\" and \"I (will) complete my Yasna\" as actions order.\"","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Yearly festivals are invoked and described as lords of the ritual males.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"Maidhyairya is identified as \"the cold,\" a holy lord of the ritual order.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Hamaspath-maedhaya is called the especial time for ritual deeds and is a holy lord of the ritual order.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"The speaker announces the Yasna to the settlements of the future one, which the future one shall produce \"as it were anew.\"","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"Praises of the Yasna are celebrated as collected, completed, and much-offered.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Myazdas of the saints of the ritual, male and female, are mentioned as objects of celebration and content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l14619-l14710","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    XII.  247 / YASNA    XII.  249 / YASNA    XIII.  251 / YASNA    XIV.  253; lines 14619-14710","start":"14619","end":"14710","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"Liturgical sections from Yasna XIV–XV in which the speaker and community worship Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, holy men and women, and various divine beings (Bountiful Immortals, Asha Vahirta, Yazads, Sraosha, etc.). The text praises Right as the best, speaks of the Kingdom belonging to Ahura and of choosing the Good Kingdom, describes sacrifices and homage performed with ritual implements, and includes a vow to dedicate one’s own body and life, together with a confession of belonging to the Mazdayasnian faith and Zarathustra’s order.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The community worships Zarathustra Spitama and also those beings—men and women—whose better service in the sacrifice is known to Ahura Mazda.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"A figure or office called the Ahu is described as excelling, and the Ratu is said to rule from the Righteous Order and to be a creator of mental goodness and of life’s actions done for Mazda.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The Kingdom is said to belong to Ahura and is associated with offering nurture to the poor.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Right, or Righteousness, is called the best and is said to bring weal to a person when that person acts rightly toward Righteousness Best.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The worshippers venerate the Ahuna-vairya and Asha Vahirta, described as a bountiful Immortal, and offer sacrifice to Ha fraoreti, identified with the confession and laudation of the Mazdayasnian Faith.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The speaker declares he will come to the Bountiful Immortals as a praiser, priest, invoker, sacrificer, memorising reciter, and chanter for their sacrifice and homage and for the dedication and sanctification of the holy prophets.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The speaker offers to dedicate the flesh of his own body and all the blessings of a prospered life to the Bountiful Immortals.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Using the Zaothra together with the Baresman, the speaker desires to approach the holy Yazads with praise and to honour all the holy lords of the ritual order—Havani, Savanghi, and Visya—at their proper times.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"The speaker openly confesses himself to be a Mazdayasnian and of Zarathustra’s order.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"A liturgical dialogue is presented in which the Zaotar speaks \"as an Ahu (revered and) chosen,\" the Ratu responds, and the Zaotar invites the Ratu, described as holy and learned, to speak forth from his Righteousness.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The speaker calls upon the Bountiful Immortals by precept and praise and with delight produced by grace, and sacrifices to them with the blessing of the good ritual and of the good Mazdayasnian Faith.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"It is said that Ahura knows whose best gift from his Righteousness belongs to the speaker in the offering.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"The speaker worships those who have lived and live ever, honouring them by their names while drawing near with praises.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"The Good Kingdom is described as a lot that is to be chosen because it most affects or bears on the worshippers’ blessings.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:15","text":"Sraosha (translated as Obedience) is invoked to be present at the rite.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"First-person worshipper-priest","description":"The speaker who declares that he comes as praiser, priest, invoker, sacrificer, reciter, and chanter to the Bountiful Immortals, dedicates his body and life’s blessings, confesses the Mazdayasnian Faith, and chooses the Good Kingdom.","role_refs":["role:1","role:8"],"evidence_refs":["ev:3","ev:4","ev:5","ev:7","ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Ahura Mazda","description":"A god who knows whose service in the sacrifice is better, to whom the Kingdom belongs, and who knows whose best gift from Righteousness is accepted in the offering.","role_refs":["role:2","role:7"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:8"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Zarathustra Spitama","description":"Called a saint and associated with an order to which the speaker confesses allegiance.","role_refs":["role:3"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:5"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Holy men and women known to Ahura","description":"Holy men and women whose better service in sacrifice is known to Ahura Mazda and who are therefore worshipped.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"Ahu","description":"A revered and It lists Mithra, Parewdi, Heroism, Sleep, ancient institutions formed before sky, water, land, plants, and the Kine, and cosmic elements such as the sea Vouru-kasha, stormy wind, and shining heaven as objects of worship. Fire is addressed as Ahura Mazda's son and lord of ritual order and is worshipped together with ritual implements like the Baresman, Zaothra, and the girdle, and with Apam-napāt, the son of waters. A later section invokes Ahura Mazda and the Bountiful Immortals in vast numbers and wishes that the Kingdom be to the one who rules best. Further sections express desire to offer homage and praise to Haomas and Zaothras, past, present, and future, described as victorious and as foes of hatred, accompanying healing virtues, religious knowledge, remedies of Mazda and Zarathustra, the Mazdayasnian Faith, prayers, truth, and the pious word against unbelief. The Haomas are described as pungent, bounteous, holy, offered and pressed with sanctity. The speaker honors strength, rectitude, blessedness, other personified powers, and the Bountiful Immortals dwelling with the Good Mind, and approaches Universal Weal and Immortality, the body and soul of the Kine, the Fire of the spoken name, and a sanctified farm-house with fields, comfort, and mercy for the poor. All of this praise is framed as sacrifice and homage to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, and the Lord that attains his ends.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Mithra of the wide pastures is explicitly named as an object of worship.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Parewdi is described as wealthy with a wealth of thoughts, a throng of words, and a breadth of actions, and is worshipped.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"A virile defensive Heroism is said to possess men who think beforehand and heroic men, to be fleeter than the fleet of the herd and men, and is worshipped.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"A footnote notes that Sleep is elsewhere an evil ruled by a demon named Bushyasta, specifying that this refers to untimely sleep.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"The text mentions 'ancient institutions' in the creation of the holy, saying they were formed before the sky, the water, the land, the plants, and the Kine of blessed gift.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The sea Vouru-kasha, the stormy wind Immortals who rule aright and dispose of all aright, and they are invoked in numbers of fifty, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, millions, and more.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The text declares that to Him who rules the best let the Kingdom be.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"The speaker desires to offer homage and praise to offered Haomas and Zaothras, including those yet to be offered, which are said to smite victoriously and be foes of hatred and to accompany healing virtues of sanctity, religious knowledge (A'isti), remedies of Mazda, remedies of Zarathustra and the Zarathu-ftrotema, and remedies belonging to a holy disciple and an itinerant versed in good devices, as well as accompanying the Mazdayasnian Faith, pious Prayer for blessings, good veracity, and the pious word against unbelief.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:13","text":"The passage lists functions such as information and explanation, preparation and devotion, libation and complete offering, and complete recital of a memorised liturgy in connection with the Haomas, Zaothras, and associated words and remedies.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"Haomas are described as pungent, bounteous, holy, offered with sanctity, yet to be offered with sanctity, being Immortals, described as ever-living, ever-helpful, male and female, dwelling together with the Good Mind.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:8"]},{"id":"obs:16","text":"The speaker desires to approach 'our Universal Weal and Immortality', the body of the Kine, and the Kine's Soul.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:17","text":"The speaker desires to approach the Fire of the spoken name and a farm-house which is sanctified and which has fields, comfort, and mercy for the poor.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:9"]},{"id":"obs:18","text":"The speaker identifies as a praiser with praise for sacrifice and homage, described as the praise of Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, and the holy and lofty Lord, and as the sacrifice and homage of the Lord that most attains his ends and of blessedness.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Mithra","description":"Mithra of the wide pastures, explicitly content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l15474-l15542","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"EN  HE    HATAM  2. / YASNA    XXI.  269 / YASNA    XXII. / YASNA    XXII.  271; lines 15474-15542","start":"15474","end":"15542","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"\"And I desire to approach this Haoma with (my) praise ... for the propitiation of Ahura Mazda, the resplendent, the glorious, and of the Bountiful Immortals\" (Yasna XXII. 20–23).","summary":"A ritual speaker invokes Immortals, Sraosha, and Ahura Mazda’s Fire, then declares a desire to approach various sanctified offerings—Haoma, milk, a sacred plant, libation waters, Haoma-water, mortars, a ritual branch, recitations of law and Gathas, prayer, wood and perfume, and all Mazda-made good objects—with praise. These items and acts are offered for the propitiation of Ahura Mazda, Fire, Bountiful Immortals, Mithra, Raman, the sun, Vayu, Mazda-given knowledge and Religion, Mathra Spenta, Zarathustrian law, Mazda-made understanding, the sacred mountain Ushi-darena, the Yazads, the Fravashis, and a Yazad of the spoken name.","language":"English","quote_policy":"quoted"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"A speaker invokes \"Immortals\", Sraosha the blessed, and Ahura Mazda's Fire, calling the Fire a \"lofty ritual lord.\"","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The speaker expresses a desire to approach Haoma with praise, describing it as lifted up with sanctity.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Milk is mentioned as fresh, \"as if living,\" and lifted up with sanctity, and is among the items the speaker approaches with praise.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The plant Hadhanaepata is described as lifted up with sanctity and is approached with praise alongside Haoma and milk.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The Zaothras are said to be for beneficial waters, containing Haoma, milk, and Hadhanaepata, and are described as lifted up with sanctity.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Haoma-water is approached with praise for the beneficial waters, and two mortars, one stone and one iron, are listed among the ritual items.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"A branch for the Baresman is approached with praise together with the memorised recital and fulfilment of the Mazdayasnian law, the heard recital of the Gathas, and a well-timed, persistent prayer for blessings uttered by the holy lord of the ritual order.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Wood and perfume belonging to Fire, called \"Ahura Mazda's son,\" and all good Mazda-made objects are offered for the propitiation of Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Mithra of the wide pastures, and Raman Zfoastra.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Propitiation is directed to the resplendent sun, described as immortal, radiant, and of fleet horses, and to Vayu, described as of predominant influence, working on high, and set over other beings in creation, with a gloss connecting Vayu’s influence to Spenta Mainyu.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The passage includes propitiation of \"the most just knowledge\" given by Mazda and of the holy and good Religion, the Mazdayasnian Faith.","category":"object","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"Mathra Spenta is described as bounteous, holy, effective, and instituted against the Daevas; together with the Zarathustrian law, the long descent of the Mazdayasnian Faith, devotion to the Mathra, and Mazda-made innate and heard understanding, these are treated as objects of propitiation.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:12","text":"Fire as Ahura Mazda’s son is again propitiated along with all fires, Mount Ushi-darena described as Mazda-made and radiant with sanctity, all holy Yazads spiritual and earthly, and the holy Fravashis, described as redoubted and overwhelming, of ancient lore and of next of kin, plus a Yazad of the spoken name.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:7"]}],"figures":[{"id":"fig:1","name_or_label":"Ritual speaker","description":"The first-person \"I\" who repeatedly desires to approach offerings with praise and to propitiate various divine beings and principles.","role_refs":["role:1"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:3","ev:4","ev:5","ev:6","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:2","name_or_label":"Ahura Mazda","description":"Deity described as \"the resplendent, the glorious\" and associated with Mazda-made good objects; Fire is called Ahura Mazda’s son, and many things are offered for this deity’s propitiation.","role_refs":["role:3","role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:4","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:3","name_or_label":"Bountiful Immortals","description":"A group of holy Immortals mentioned as recipients of propitiation together with Ahura Mazda.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"fig:4","name_or_label":"Sraosha the blessed","description":"Named as a blessed being invoked along with Immortals and Ahura Mazda’s Fire.","role_refs":["role:4"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"fig:5","name_or_label":"Fire, Ahura Mazda's son","description":"Personified Fire described as Ahura Mazda’s Fire, a \"lofty ritual lord\" and \"Ahura Mazda's son,\" receiving wood, perfume, and propitiation together with all fires.","role_refs":["role:4","role:9"],"evidence_refs":["ev:1","ev:4","ev:7"]},{"id":"fig:6","name_or_label":"Haoma","description":"A sacred substance approached with praise and described as lifted up with sanctity; also present in the Zaothras and Haoma-water.","role_refs":["role:2"],"evidence_refs":["ev:2","ev:3"]},{"id":"fig:7","name_or_label":"Milk","description":"Milk described as fresh, as Let the Mazdayasnian pray for a smiter who may quickly destroy the demon who causes their decrease.","summary":"A fragmentary ritual passage describes the moons of the season waning and attributes their decrease to a malignant female demon. A Mazdayasnian worshipper is urged to pray for a smiter to destroy her, and it is said that her adherents cannot maintain her by prayers. The demon is portrayed as mighty, weapon-bearing, and wandering in her strength, with an address to Zarathustra. A note explains that the text was to be spoken when a vessel containing the Zaothras was taken in hand, and another note remarks that the fragment is grammatically corrupt and conjecturally translated.","language":"English","quote_policy":"quoted"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The moons of the season are said to wane.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The Mazdayasnian worshipper is instructed to pray for a smiter who may quickly destroy the demon responsible for the moons' decrease.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The text expresses a wish that the malignant one die off quickly.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"It is stated that none of the demon's adherents can maintain this Druj(k) by prayers.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The female demon is described as smiting fiercely with her weapon.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"She is said to go on and to have been most mighty.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"She wanders on, mindful of her might, and becomes strong in proportion as she content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l14520-l14616","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    XL  245 / YASNA    XII.  247 / YASNA    XII.  249 / YASNA    XIII.  251; lines 14520-14616","start":"14520","end":"14616","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"The passage is a litany of invocations and offerings. The speaker first invokes various human leaders, then the Mazdayasnian Faith personified as Pare^di, chief of women, and the holy earth. Next, he invokes the Fire of Ahura Mazda, lords of holy men who care for cattle and fields, and other leaders such as thrifty tillers and charioteers, along with the chief of the fire-priest, the Atharvan and his pupils, the Bountiful Immortals, prophets, fire-priests, warriors, and tillers. The prophets are praised for their wisdom and doctrinal exactness. The worshipper then addresses the Bountiful Immortals, offering the flesh of his own body and the blessings of his life. A brief statement mentions \"the two spirits\" who thought, spoke, and acted, followed by praise of Ahura Mazda for thinking, speaking, disposing, and doing all good things, to whom the worshippers pledge homage, sacrifices, gifts, and prayers with confessions of debt. Finally, they say they approach Ahura Mazda by the kinship of good kindred, Righteousness, thrift-law, and Piety, and they worship the Fravashi of the Kine of blessed gift, of Gaya Maretan, and a general holy Fravashi.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The speaker invokes several human lords, including a house-lord and chiefs of various lords, as well as the chief of women identified with the Mazdayasnian Faith and Pare^di, and also invokes the holy earth that bears humans.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Pare^di, representing the Mazdayasnian Faith, is described as blessed and good and as the holy one of humankind, with a footnote glossing her as a goddess of riches.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The speaker invokes the Fire of Ahura Mazda, calling it the lord of friendly and helpful persons, together with energetic lords of holy men who are strenuous in caring for cattle and fields, and invokes the chief of the thrifty tiller, a steady settler of sanctity, and the chief of the charioteer.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The speaker invokes the chief of the fire-priest by means of the sciences of the Mazdayasnian Faith, invokes the chief of the Atharvan and his pupils and their lords, and summons the Bountiful Immortals and prophets.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The prophets are characterized as the wisest, most scrupulous and exact in uttering words of doctrine and service, most devoted to their duties, and most glorious in their thoughts.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","

content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l14928-l15079","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"YASNA    XVII. / YASNA    XIX.  259 / YASNA    XVIII4. / YASNA    XIX.; lines 14928-15079","start":"14928","end":"15079","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"A brief prayer asks Mazda, maker of the kine, plants, and waters, to grant immortality and weal. A commentary on the Ahuna-vairya formula then paraphrases its opening, praising the excellence of the Ahu and the Ratu and speaking of Ahura's kingdom, which provides a nurturer for the poor. Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda which word he declared that existed before the sky, water, earth, cattle, plants, fire, humans, Daevas, Khrafstra-men, and the entire corporeal world. Ahura replies that it was the Ahuna-vairya, which he pronounced before the creation of heaven, waters, land, animals, plants, fire (called Ahura Mazda's son), humans, Daevas, Khrafstra-men, and all good creatures containing the seed of righteousness. He explains that the parts of this formula especially belong to him and that each correctly recited part is worth a hundred other prominent ritual stanzas, while even an imperfect recitation counts as ten. Whoever mentally recalls and recites the formula, worshipping thus, will have their soul brought by Ahura Mazda with threefold safety and speed over the Bridge of Alnva/ to heaven (the best life), to Righteousness the Best, and to the lights of heaven; but whoever omits portions while reciting will have their soul withdrawn from the better world as far as the earth is large and wide. Ahura states that he pronounced this saying, containing its Ahu and its Ratu, before the creation of heaven, waters, plants, cattle, humans, and the sun made for the acquisition of the creation of the Bountiful Immortals. The more bountiful of the two Spirits (Ahura) is said to have declared to Zarathustra the entire pure creation—what exists, what is coming into being, and what shall be—regarding a life devoted to Mazda, and the word is described as the most emphatic of all utterances ever spoken, now spoken, or yet to be spoken.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"A speaker addresses Mazda, described as maker of the kine, plants, and waters, asking to be granted immortality and weal.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The commentary paraphrases the Ahuna-vairya formula, saying that as the Ahu is excellent, so is the Ratu, a ruler from the righteous Order, a creator of mental goodness and of life's actions done for Mazda.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The kingdom is said to belong to Ahura and to offer a nurturer to the poor.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda which word he declared that existed before the sky, water, earth, cattle, plants, fire, the holy man, the Daevas, the Khrafstra-men, and the entire incarnate world, before all good creatures made by Mazda that contain the seed of righteousness.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"Ahura Mazda answers that the word was the Ahuna-vairya formula, which he pronounced for Spitama Zarathustra before the sky, the waters, the land, the cattle, the plants, the fire (called Ahura Mazda's son), the holy man, the Daevas, the Khrafstra-men, and the entire corporeal world and good creatures made by Mazda.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Ahura Mazda says that the parts of the Ahuna-vairya especially belong to him and that when each part is intoned aloud correctly, without needless repetition or omission, it is worth a hundred other prominent ritual stanzas, while an imperfect recitation with additions and omissions is equivalent to ten such stanzas.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The practice of recalling a portion of the Ahuna-vairya mentally, undertoning it, or reciting it aloud is described as a form of worship.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Ahura Mazda promises that whoever recalls and recites the Ahuna-vairya in this way will have their soul brought creation.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"A well-timed prayer for blessings is described as praise of the Mathra Spenta (bounteous word Her waters, equal in bulk to all earthly waters, flow from the high mountain Hukairya to the sea Vouru-kasha, stirring its gulfs, with a thousand tributaries and outlets, and a chief outlet that distributes waters to all seven Karshvars in all seasons. Zarathuitra is instructed to declare the Bountiful Immortals' sacrificial words so that waters, plants, the Fravashis of the saints, and the created Yazads (heavenly and earthly, holy and beneficent) may receive offerings. A speaker confesses himself a Mazda-worshipper and offers praise, propitiation, and sacrifice to Thraetaona Athwyan and his Fravashi, the saint and holy lord of ritual order, while praying to be free from dog Kuro, Tarewani, and Karpan and identifying with those who \"sacrifice in order\"; other prayers such as the Ahuna, Ahem, and Ahmai raesha are said to follow, invoking sacrifice, homage, strength, and swiftness to Thraetaona's Fravashi. Another fragment proclaims the Airyma-ishyo as the greatest authoritative prayer, most influential and helpful for progress, which the Saoshyants should use and revere. content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l18535-l18648","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"VISPARAD  II2. / VISPARAD    II.  339 / VISPARAD    III.  34I / VISPARAD    III.; lines 18535-18648","start":"18535","end":"18648","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"The passage opens the Haoma offering with praise to ritual lords and, using the Zaothra and Baresman, seeks Ahura’s revealed lore and pastoral blessing. It then gives a roll-call in which the Zaotar and Ratu summon various priestly officials and exemplary members of the community—warrior, farmer, householders, youth, women, and a learned holy man—to participate in the rite.","summary":"Within a Visparad section, the speaker praises Fshusho-mathra and Hadhaokhdha as holy lords of the ritual order. With the Zaothra and Baresman, he declares his desire to approach a question put to Ahura and the divine lore revealed in response, along with the farmhouse, pastures, blessed cattle, and a holy cattle-breeding man. A heading announces the beginning of the Haoma offering and the priestly roll-call. The Zaotar calls for ritual officials—Havanan, Atare-vakhsha, Frabaretar, Aberej, Asnatar, Raethwi-rkar, Sraoshavareza—and the Ratu answers that he will come, while translator notes identify these as priests handling Haoma, fire, offerings, water, washing, purification, and penance. The Zaotar further summons a Fire-priest, warrior, thrifty tiller of the earth, house-lord, and lords of the clan and district, as well as a morally exemplary youth (married within his kin), a province-ranger, an itinerant of many arts, and a house-mistress. He then calls a pious woman advanced in holy thoughts, words, and deeds, well subordinated to her holy lord and likened to bounteous Aramaiti, along with Ahura’s wives, and finally a holy man advanced in good thoughts, words, and deeds, learned in pious lore, innocent of Kayadha, whose actions promote the righteous order in the settlements.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"Praise is directed to Fshusho-mathra and to the lofty lord Hadhaokhdha as holy lords of the ritual order.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"Fshusho-mathra and Hadhaokhdha are explicitly called holy lords of the ritual order.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"With the Zaothra and Baresman, the speaker states a desire to approach the question asked of Ahura and the lore of the Lord which he reveals in answer.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"The intention also includes the farmhouse of a man with pastures, the pasture produced for blessed the priest.","category":"setting","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"During the roll-call, the Zaotar calls for ritual offices such as Havanan, Atare-vakhsha, Frabaretar, and Aberej to be present, and the Ratu replies to each call with a promise to come.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"A note explains that the Ratu answers on behalf of all offices house-mistress.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:10"]},{"id":"obs:14","text":"A note remarks that marriage within kin was an important custom treated in a lost content.text: {"record_id":"batch.motif.zoroastrian-avesta-yasna-gathas-mills-archive-l19124-l19216","source_text_path":"texts/public-domain/zoroastrian/project-gutenberg/zend-avesta-part-3-yasna-gathas.md","passage_locator":{"label":"VISPARAD    III. / VISPARAD    IV.  343 / VISPARAD    XI.  351 / VISPARAD    XII.  353; lines 19124-19216","start":"19124","end":"19216","translation":"The Zend-Avesta, Part III: The Yasna, Visparad, Afrinagan, Gahs, and Miscellaneous Fragments","notes":"Stable markdown line range generated from canonical text."},"canonical_text":{"quote":"","summary":"A priestly speaker invokes Blessedness, Nairya-sangha, Victorious Peace, Ahura Mazda’s Fire, and the lofty Lord, offering sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise for the holy and clean creation. He declares that he, following Ahura Mazda and Zarathustra, makes known the Avesta and ritual prescriptions, addressing the Bountiful Immortals and describing the celebrants as holy Saoshyants who pray for blessings, victory, sanctification, and the well-being of their souls. A subsequent section speaks of Haoma libations offered to Ahura Mazda and Zarathustra, which bring abundance in cattle and men and are associated with the protective Sraosha. The text describes wise offerings of the Ahuna-vairya formula, precise ritual actions with Haoma and mortars, correctly practiced ceremonies, and spread Baresmans, all belonging to the doctrines and recitations of the Mazdayasnian religion. These ritual deeds are said to be full of devices and wisdom, delivered by Ahura Mazda, nourished by Vohu Manah and grown from the Righteous Order, and the speakers hope to be among those of Spenta Mainyu’s world by imparting these teachings to the chosen.","language":"English","quote_policy":"summarized"},"literal_observations":[{"id":"obs:1","text":"The text invokes Blessedness, Nairya-sangha, Victorious Peace, Ahura Mazda’s Fire, and the lofty Lord, offering them sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise directed to the entire creation of the holy and the clean.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:1"]},{"id":"obs:2","text":"The speaker states that they make known what is lifted up in offering, identified with the Avesta, as Ahura Mazda directed it should be said and as Zarathustra directed.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"The speaker identifies himself as a priest acquainted with sacrifice and homage, who understands the lawful and legitimate Avesta and the ritual prescriptions for sacrifice, homage, and propitiation.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:4","text":"Addressing the Bountiful Immortals, the priest describes prayers for blessings, victory, sanctification, and the well-being of souls, and says that the celebrants are the holy Saoshyants.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"The speaker says that these things are made known in their celebrations and offered to Ahura Mazda, described as the greatest of all, the master and the Lord.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:3"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"Haoma offerings are poured in libation to the lofty Lord Ahura Mazda and to the holy Zarathustra Spitama and are said to produce abundance in cattle and in men.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:7","text":"The abundance produced by the Haoma offerings is likened to the good Sraosha, who accompanies the worshippers with great splendour of sanctity and is asked to be present with energetic effort to aid their worship.","category":"relationship","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:8","text":"Wise offerings of the Ahuna-vairya formula are offered; these utterances are described as intoned with sanctity and possessing many teachings of religious wisdom.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:9","text":"Two mortars are described as pouring out the Haomas and being pushed forward with precision as part of the ritual action.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:10","text":"The text enumerates correctly spoken words, Zarathustrian utterances, correctly practiced movements.","category":"sequence","evidence_refs":["ev:6"]},{"id":"obs:11","text":"The ritual deeds and teachings are said to become full of devices and wisdom, to have their nourishment from Vohu Two mortars, one of stone and one of iron, are addressed and asked to be full of wisest meaning as they serve Mazdayasnian households and communities, appearing with wood-billets, perfumes, and blessings. The text then describes worship ‘according to the ritual’ of Ahura Mazda and the Bountiful Immortals, and sacrificial offerings directed to the correctly spoken sacrificial word (Mathra), to Zarathustra as possessor of the Mathra, to blessings for the saints, and to a hail addressed to the Bountiful Immortals. The Ahuna-vairya formula is also worshipped as holy lord of the ritual order with its Ahu and Ratu, and sacrifices are made to all constituent parts of the Gatha Ahunavaiti and their recitation. Finally, the Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians are exhorted to ready their feet, hands, and understanding for lawful deeds in accordance with sacred Order, to avoid unlawful and evil deeds contrary to the
